title: A scope-trait model is read through the composed scoped query, never a raw query built from scratch
intent: A model that mixes a soft-delete or tenant-scope trait carries row scope. A bespoke read that queries the model directly — instead of building on the composed scoped query — drops that scope, leaking soft-deleted or cross-tenant rows (closing the composition point to overrides did not close a new read method that never calls it). Build reads on the scoped query and the declared filter seam; the request session applies the scope to every ORM read as the runtime backstop (the mapped entities a statement reaches through its columns, joins, predicates and nested selects, aggregates included), and this rule is the build-time early warning. A read the session cannot scope (a scoped table read through its Core table, literal SQL) is refused when it runs rather than answered unscoped. The one sanctioned raw query — the scoped composition point itself — lives in the framework, not a module, so it is never scanned here.
reference: select(Model) on a SoftDeleteMixin / TenantScopedMixin model is refused in modules (ADR 0017, F1); build on base_query() / business_filters(), with apply_row_scope as the runtime backstop.

runtime.rationale: The request session scopes every ORM read at execution: apply_row_scope's predicates are applied as loader criteria to each mapped entity the statement reaches, in its columns, joins, predicates and nested selects, aggregates included. A bespoke select(Model), or an aggregate over a scoped model, that skipped base_query() is filtered for soft-delete and the registered predicates at execution, so the leak the rule warns about is closed even when the source pattern slips through. A read the session cannot scope is refused before it runs with UnscopedReadError (ADR 0204 decision 6): a SELECT that reads a scoped table through its Core table (a column, a join, a subquery, an alias or sample of it, table() in any case or schema), literal SQL wherever the statement writes it, and a FROM element the session does not know. An entity named in a loader option, a VALUES row or a column property is scoped there like any other. Only the shapes it can scope pass, so a new shape is refused rather than read. A view or a function in the database is read by its name, like any table or function, so it scopes the rows it reads in its own SQL.
